label: early copy steps (recall 1-2) when u/j is about to be output
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at the first two copy steps after the delimiter (recall_idx 1: 75% of mass, recall_idx 2: 24%; never in the original phase, at the delimiter step, or at recall_idx >= 4). Within those steps it is content-gated by the tokens about to be recalled: strongest when u or j (and to a lesser degree p, g, 2, b) sit among the next few original tokens (next_out=u has lift 12.6x, j 8x). Top activations are sequences like r u u u u / n j u u u, where several u/j tokens follow orig(0). Rate rises with t and with the number of outputs left. The predicate (recall 1-2 and u/j in the next three recalled positions) gets about 82% of mass on dev but only about 35% precision, because many of those steps stay inactive and many weak activations have no u/j coming up, so the content dependence is graded rather than crisp. It does not depend on the input token itself or on digit count.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=u (+4.63), orig3=u (+4.47), orig4=u (+4.04), orig2=j (+3.71), orig3=j (+3.35), orig5=u (+3.28). Lower it: in_first=1 (-5.17), orig3=l (-4.77), recall_idx=5 (-4.41), orig3=x (-3.76).
